input.quote: 9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement or an affected Order Form for the other Party's material breach if the breach remains uncured thirty days after written notice describing it in reasonable detail.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause, insolvency and incident-based termination (9.1–9.3), and 8.1 fixes a three-year term with twelve-month Order Form renewals (8.2). No convenience termination right exists for Customer anywhere (27.3 is force-majeure specific; 6.2, 19.4 and 20.5 are remedy-based), which is a deviation in a term longer than 12 months. Retained 10.2 refunds only "prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination", which is narrower than prepaid Fees as defined in 1.5 and is not an express pro-rata refund, so it does not satisfy the refund element. We therefore insert a single new 9.4 carrying all four preferred elements: a Customer convenience right over the Agreement or any Order Form, thirty days' written notice, a pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express bar on Vendor convenience termination during a committed term. Fallback is unavailable at 30 days' notice, so the cure is drafted at the preferred level.

proposal.summary: Add Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and bar Vendor convenience termination during a committed term
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The three-year term leaves us no exit without cause, so we added a Customer convenience right on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and confirmed Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.

ops.text: 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor may not terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
